content.content:
The user asks: "Which of the world's five highest mountains were first successfully climbed by British mountaineers?" The world's five highest mountains are the eight-thousanders: Everest (8848 m), K2 (8611 m), Kangchenjunga (8586 m), Lhotse (8516 m), Makalu (8485 m). Actually the five highest are: Everest, K2, Kangchenjunga, Lhotse, Makalu.

We need to know which of these were first ascended by British mountaineers. Let's recall: Everest first ascent 1953 by Sir Edmund Hillary (NZ) and Tenzing Norgay (Sherpa) – not British (though Hillary was New Zealander, but part of British Commonwealth). Not British.

K2 first ascent 1954 by Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni (Italian). Not British.

Kangchenjunga first ascent 1955 by Joe Brown and George Band – British (both British). So yes.

Lhotse first ascent 1956 by a Swiss/Austrian team (Ernst Reiss, Fritz Luchsinger) – not British.

Makalu first ascent 1955 by a French expedition (Jean Franco, Lionel Terray) – not British.

Thus only Kangchenjunga was first climbed by British mountaineers. However, check if any other of the top five have British first ascents? Let's double-check: The first ascent of Everest by British? Actually first attempt was British 1924 (Mallory). Not successful. British did not succeed until 1953 with Hillary (NZ). So not British.

Thus answer: Kangchenjunga.

But the question: "Which of the world's five highest mountains were first successfully climbed by British mountaineers?" Could be plural, but answer is just Kangchenjunga.

Provide details: year 1955, team members, etc.

Let's answer succinctly.

content:
The only one of the world’s five highest peaks that was first summited by a British team is **Kangchenjunga** (8 586 m).

| Mountain | Height | First successful ascent | Nationality of the climbers who made the first ascent |
|----------|--------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| **Kangchenjunga** | 8 586 m | 25 May 1955 | **British** – Joe Brown and George Band (part of the 1955 Commonwealth Expedition) |
| Everest | 8 848 m | 29 May 1953 | New Zealander (Sir Edmund Hillary) & Sherpa (Tenzing Norgay) |
| K2 | 8 611 m | 31 July 1954 | Italians (Lino Lacedelli & Achille Compagnoni) |
| Lhotse | 8 516 m | 18 May 1956 | Swiss (Ernst Reiss & Fritz Luchsinger) |
| Makalu | 8 485 m | 15 May 1955 | French (Jean Franco & Lionel Terray) |

So, among the five highest mountains on Earth, **Kangchenjunga** is the sole peak whose first successful summit was achieved by British mountaineers.
